questions.q: What is the practical difference between the Apex Developer Guide and the Apex Reference Guide?
options: The Developer Guide is narrative and concept-based; the Reference Guide is a class-by-class, method-by-method lookup
They are two names for the exact same document
The Reference Guide only covers triggers, while the Developer Guide covers everything else
The Developer Guide is for Trailhead only and has no connection to developer.salesforce.com
questions.explain: The Developer Guide teaches concepts narratively, while the Reference Guide is organized for looking up a specific class or method's exact signature and behavior.

questions.q: Why does it matter that Apex documentation is versioned by API version?
options: It doesn't matter; all versions of the documentation are identical
API versioning only affects Visualforce, never Apex
A method, governor limit, or piece of syntax can genuinely differ between platform releases, so reading an outdated version's page can give you incorrect current information
Only sandboxes have versioned documentation; production always uses one fixed version
questions.explain: Salesforce ships new releases multiple times a year, and behavior or limits can change between them, so confirming you're reading documentation matching your actual org's API version matters for accuracy.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend as the most reliable way to check your org's actual current governor limit consumption?
options: Memorizing the numbers from a tutorial you read once
Assuming every org has identical limits with no need to check
Asking a coworker to estimate it
Using the Limits class at runtime, since it reflects your org's real configuration directly
questions.explain: The Limits class (covered in Lesson 26) checks the running transaction's actual consumption and ceiling directly, which is more reliable than a memorized or outdated figure.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what role does Trailhead best play relative to the Reference Guide?
options: Trailhead replaces the Reference Guide entirely and should always be used instead
Trailhead is a good conceptual on-ramp for learning a topic, but the Reference Guide is the primary source for exact current method syntax
Trailhead and the Reference Guide cover completely unrelated topics
Trailhead is only for Visualforce, never for Apex
questions.explain: Trailhead is positioned as a conceptual learning tool, while the Reference Guide is the primary source to confirm exact, current method signatures and behavior.

questions.q: What habit does this lesson recommend before shipping code that uses an unfamiliar method?
options: Look up the method in the Reference Guide first, confirm its exact signature and usage notes, and then write the code
Write the code first based on memory, and only check documentation if it fails in production
Avoid using any method that isn't covered in this course
Ask an AI assistant and treat its answer as authoritative with no further verification
questions.explain: The habit this lesson teaches is verifying unfamiliar syntax against the official Reference Guide before writing code that depends on it, rather than discovering a mismatch later.
